claims.head: Something has to give
claims.body: The Oilers are the league’s best for the power play, but the Hurricanes are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Oilers’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays, and Carolina has had one of the league’s best penalty kills for years.

claims.head: Power against power
claims.call: The Oilers’ L1 (Draisaitl, McDavid and Podkolzin) spends at least 55% of its 5-on-5 time against the Hurricanes’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Oilers keep sending McDavid’s line (Draisaitl, McDavid and Podkolzin) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Mike Babcock has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Hurricanes’ first line is Carrier, Aho and Svechnikov.

notes.text: Seth Jarvis is out and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward. William Carrier has taken his spot beside Sebastian Aho and Andrei Svechnikov.
Taylor Hall is out (upper-body injury) and missed their last game.
Jordan Staal is out 1-2 months (calf tear) and has missed the last 2 games. Mark Jankowski has taken his spot beside Jordan Martinook and Nikolaj Ehlers.
Alexander Nikishin has not played this season. He is a top-four defenseman. Mike Reilly has taken his spot beside Shayne Gostisbehere.
Logan Stankoven has started killing penalties: on the ice for 31% of the team’s shorthanded time in 8 games, up from 1% last season.

faceoff.text: Jordan Staal is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 46% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 20 seconds at a time, against 64 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by Nikolaj Ehlers (17 of 20 changes).

notes.text: Zach Hyman has not dressed for the last 6 games. He is a top-six forward.
Ryan Nugent-Hopkins is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward.
Matt Savoie is on long-term injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has not played this season. Leon Draisaitl has taken his spot beside Connor McDavid and Vasily Podkolzin.
Filip Hållander joined from PIT on Oct 7 and has played beside Jason Dickinson and Kasperi Kapanen.
Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 59% of the team’s power-play time in 7 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 3% of the team’s shorthanded time in 5 games, down from 30% last season.

EDM.head: A slightly uphill night for the Oilers
EDM.body: Even though Edmonton has home-ice advantage and gets Hyman back, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Oilers can tip it if they get good looks.

CAR.head: Leaning the Hurricanes’ way
CAR.body: Even though Edmonton has home-ice advantage and gets Hyman back, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Oilers can still swing it if they get good looks.

story.head: Can anyone stop the Hurricanes?
paras: The Oilers are 5-1-1. The Hurricanes are on a tear, six straight wins.

It’s strength against strength: the Oilers are the league’s best for the power play, but the Hurricanes are one of the best at the penalty kill. At home, Mike Babcock likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Canes’ first line.

items.text: The Oilers are newly without Frederik Andersen, have been without Zach Hyman since Sep 29, and have had to make do without Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Matt Savoie all season. Devon Levi is expected to start.
The Hurricanes are newly without Taylor Hall and Jordan Staal, and have had to make do without Seth Jarvis and Alexander Nikishin all season.
Nikolaj Ehlers has a point in five straight games against Edmonton.
Connor McDavid has a point in six straight games against Carolina, and 11 points in his last six against them.
